pages.title: What is Citadel
pages.description: Citadel is Minefort's Luau scripting engine for Minecraft servers — one pack runs unchanged on every Java client from 1.8 to 26.x, as the whole game (lite mode) or as a plugin over survival (full mode).

pages.title: Quick start
pages.description: Build a first Citadel pack from scratch — manifest, script, terrain, a join handler, a command — then run it, edit it live, and understand what the reload did.

pages.title: Tooling
pages.description: Set up luau-lsp with Citadel's type definitions for autocomplete and strict type checking, and use the citadel CLI to run, check, generate and render packs.

pages.title: Luau primer
pages.description: The Luau language in one page, for developers coming from JavaScript, Python or Java — syntax, tables as objects, types, strict mode, and the parts of standard Lua that Citadel leaves out.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.description: How a Citadel server is put together — the main room, per-room tables, ticks and the scheduler, chunks and loading, the pack lifecycle, and what happens on reload.

pages.title: Pack anatomy
pages.description: Everything in a Citadel pack — the citadel.yml manifest key by key, the file layout, sounds and other assets, dimensions, permissions groups, and where the world and its data live on disk.

pages.title: Runtime
pages.description: The script runtime in detail — task.spawn/wait/delay/defer semantics, the initialization exception, require and modules, the tick budget, what reload keeps and discards.

pages.title: The event model
pages.description: How every on_* subscription works — connections and cancellation, the notification events across world, players and rooms, and the three cancellable asks with their two-millisecond deadline.

pages.title: Conventions
pages.description: The rules every Citadel API call follows — namespaces, vec3 positions, colours and colour names, text runs, options tables with strict field checking, the nil/false/true tri-state, and the spelling invariants.

pages.title: Rooms and dimensions
pages.description: Two ways to have more than one world — rooms, made at runtime with rooms.create and each with its own world/players/ui/game tables, and dimensions, declared in citadel.yml and reached by routes and player:travel.

pages.title: Terrain generation
pages.description: Making chunks with world.on_generate and world.on_populate, the Chunk API, biomes, noise, the a0.1.0 terrain steps in citadel.yml, and declaring a whole world with world.generate rules.

pages.title: Block reference
pages.description: Block naming in Citadel — canonical names without the namespace, [property=value] states in any order and subset, version fallbacks with | alternatives, the write and read calls, player heads with skins, and the detail = 2 half-block system.

pages.title: Building
pages.description: world.build and the Builder API, Schematic values, pasting with world.paste and chunk:paste, turning, cropping and replacing builds, .schem import, the render/check workflow, craft advice for building well, and named parts with build mode.

pages.title: Custom blocks
pages.description: game.blocks.define makes a pack's own blocks — the definition fields, states and block.data, the eleven hooks with their exact callbacks, extends and the base() protocol, missed-deadline behaviour, redstone power, and textures and models for 1.21.4+ clients.

pages.title: Game data
pages.description: The game registry a pack reads — game.block(name) and its fields, the block drops switch, game.item, entity kinds with their facts, the spawn/attacks/interact tri-state fields and their resolution rules, and game.terrain.

pages.title: World state
pages.description: The room-level switches and clocks — world.rules with its seven boolean rules and read/write semantics, the time of day with world.time, weather, world.explode, and where players arrive with world.spawn_point.

pages.title: Zones, raycasts and paths
pages.description: Querying space — trigger zones with on_enter/on_leave, single and batched raycasts, line-of-sight checks, the mob pathfinder, light at a position, and nearby-player queries.

pages.title: Custom entities
pages.description: Defining your own entity kinds with game.entities.define — looks, physics, size, persist, the living body, hit volumes, flying, and the on_think brain — plus amending the game's own kinds.

pages.title: Entity handles
pages.description: The EntityHandle API — the live handle world.spawn returns, world.entities lists and every hook receives: position and rotation, velocity and push, nearby queries, e.data, and life checks.

pages.title: Mobs and spawning
pages.description: Putting mobs in the world with world.spawn, how a mob acts on its own on both kinds of server, the per-kind spawn tri-state, and what mobs drop.

pages.title: NPCs
pages.description: world.npc and the Npc API — skins, name tags, poses, walking, holding items, armour and riding — plus world.puppet, a mob body with no mind of its own that the script moves.

pages.title: Player lifecycle
pages.description: The four player events — on_join, on_leave, on_death and on_respawn — the one player value and its per-session data table, what survives a reconnect, and moving a player to another server with player:connect.

pages.title: Movement and cameras
pages.description: Moving players — teleport, move_to, travel, push, and the writable speed, scale and reach — riding and seats, body rotation, the four camera modes with camera.path easing, and the input events a pack can read.

pages.title: Inventory and items
pages.description: ItemSpec forms — a name or a table with count, name, lore, colours, glint, canvas, id, damage, model and skin — the give/take/count/inventory/held calls, pack items, head items, armour via wear, and recipes.

pages.title: Visibility and teams
pages.description: Who sees whom — player.visible removes a body from every client, viewer:hide removes it from one viewer only, and can_see reads the two together; what hidden means, how long it lasts and what a new session resets.

pages.title: Health and damage
pages.description: player.health, max_health, food and saturation — nil where the game version has no rule, the 1..1024 maximum, healing and respawn — plus player:damage, the death causes, the damage/fall/survival room rules and PvP through players.on_click.

pages.title: Permissions
pages.description: Permission nodes — wildcards, a leading minus, most-specific-wins — groups in the pack's citadel.yml with inheritance, putting players in groups from script until they leave, operators with every node, and gating commands with player:has.

pages.title: UI basics
pages.description: Chat lines, titles and subtitles, the action bar, boss bars, the sidebar and the tab list — the ui global and player.ui — plus the text-run system, colour names and moving text that every text surface shares.

pages.title: Screens and layouts
pages.description: world.screen — a wall or floor of map frames drawn on pixel by pixel, with click hooks and per-player views — and the layout system that puts a HUD of boxes, images and labels on the client's own screen.

pages.title: Canvases and pictures
pages.description: world.canvas — a picture of one or more maps with no frame of its own, shown on frames, in hands and on screens — plus frame displays, the map palette, and video, live-stream and streamed-sound playback.

pages.title: Menus
pages.description: player.ui.menu — a titled grid of up to 54 items every client draws, chest on Java and form on Bedrock — and the hotbar as a per-player menu of nine items with live canvas maps.

pages.title: Dialogs
pages.description: player.ui.dialog — a screen of boxes, words and pictures built from ui.kit, live-redrawn after every click. Needs Java 1.21.6, a declared dialogs flag in citadel.yml, and a client that took the resource pack.

pages.title: Displays and models
pages.description: world.display — floating text, items, blocks, frames and 3D models with live fields, tweening and billboards — plus the models.new system of materials, textures, parts, boxes, named animations and vehicles.

pages.title: Particles and lasers
pages.description: fx.particle — particles at points, one call or many, with count, spread, velocity, speed and dust colour and size — and the beam pattern: dust along a line, redrawn every other tick, tweenable into a laser.

pages.title: Sound
pages.description: sound.play and player:sound for short effects through the client's resource pack, sound.stop, and sound.stream — music, ambience and radios through Simple Voice Chat, from speakers that move or no place at all.

pages.title: Commands
pages.description: commands.add builds slash commands from a usage line — the argument types and ranges, permission nodes, aliases, tab-completion suggestions with tooltips, one name with several shapes, and what /help shows.

pages.title: Storage
pages.description: The per-pack local JSON store — storage.get/set/keys by key in the pack's storage.json, what a JSON value may be, the UTF-8 rule, atomic writes, and storage.status/flush for when a write fails.

pages.title: Shared stores
pages.description: The experience-wide durable store — stores.open and the DurableStore calls, versions and conflict errors, fencing-token leases, player blobs, every size limit, and the rules of calling a store that yields.

pages.title: Network
pages.description: An experience of more than one server — members, labels and instances; network.start/find/status, on_instance and on_gone, the instance table, how player:connect moves players, failures with reasons, and every limit.

pages.title: HTTP
pages.description: http.get fetches public URLs with headers, timeout and an on-disk cache; the answer is an HttpResponse with :json() and :image(). Plus http.socket WebSockets, the queue limits, and fetching chunk terrain live.

pages.title: Shop
pages.description: Selling products for Gems — shop.prompt and shop.owns, the on_paid delivery contract with its all-handlers-must-succeed acknowledgement, on_declined, product keys, and the retry and idempotence rules.

pages.title: Hub
pages.description: What Minefort tells its own hub — hub.servers, hub.experiences and hub.hubs with their fields, hub.role ranks and hub.online, banners read through the http cache, and the rent/point portal calls.

pages.title: Server settings
pages.description: The server's citadel.yml — mode, packs, the bind addresses for Java, resource packs, Bedrock RakNet and NetherNet, game, world_dir, operators, online_mode, nethernet_tls and store_dir; the mode decision order and how a player's identity is decided.

pages.title: Limits
pages.description: The tick budget — budget_ms and its 2 ms default, what it covers and what keeps the 100 ms runaway limit instead, what happens when it runs out, citadel.budget() fields, citadel.on_slow, the 4096-event queue, and the asks the engine asks.

pages.title: Build a cottage
pages.description: Code a cottage — plinth, walls, set-back windows, gable roof, garden — as one world.build with named parts, paste it into generated ground, and check it with the citadel CLI.

pages.title: Coin rush
pages.description: Build a sixty-second arcade game — a round arena, gold plates taken by walking on them, a boss-bar countdown, live sidebar scores, and best scores kept in storage.

pages.title: Parkour, a room each
pages.description: Give every player a world of their own — /play makes a room with a random twelve-jump course, a live timer, gold checkpoints, an emerald finish, and a best time in storage.

pages.title: A dungeon dimension
pages.description: Add a second world to a pack — declare a dungeon dimension in citadel.yml, generate mossy corridors under a bedrock roof, step on a carpet to travel in, and /leave to come back.

pages.title: Scoreboard with a button
pages.description: A compact tutorial — a screen in the air, a Tap me item on the hotbar: right-click it, a hat sound plays, and every player's tap count redraws on the board, kept in storage.

pages.title: Cooldowns
pages.description: Rate-limit commands and actions with player.data and time.now — per-player cooldowns that survive reloads safely and degrade correctly.

pages.title: Leaderboards
pages.description: Three leaderboard patterns — the live sidebar for a running game, the world.screen board that persists with storage, and the experience-wide best score with stores:increment.

pages.title: Teleport pads
pages.description: Three ways to move players between places — world.zone trigger pads in a room, routes between dimensions with a standing trigger, and commands for explicit travel.

pages.title: Kits
pages.description: Give players starter kits with player:give — inventory merging rules, taking items back, replacing the whole loadout, and hotbar shortcuts for one-click kits.

pages.title: Teams
pages.description: Set up teams with player.data, make members visible only to their own team, and keep the assignments alive across joins and reloads.

pages.title: A minigame loop
pages.description: The round-based minigame skeleton — a room per round with rooms.create, a countdown on time.every with a boss bar, scores in player.data, and cleanup when the last player leaves.

pages.title: Save and load
pages.description: Choosing and using the three persistence layers — player.data for the session, storage for the pack, stores for the experience — with flush, conflict and reload rules in one place.

pages.title: Event catalog
pages.description: Every on_* event in the Citadel API in one table — what fires it, what the handler receives, and where the full treatment lives.

pages.title: Client versions
pages.description: The player:supports feature matrix — which client version each UI and world feature needs, how resource-pack refusals read, and what min_client does.

pages.title: FAQ and troubleshooting
pages.description: The questions that come up when a pack misbehaves — load failures, silent reloads, mobs that do not spawn, commands that vanish, stores that error, and what the log is telling you.

pages.title: Limits
pages.description: Every numeric limit in Citadel in one table — tick budgets, load times, event queues, stores, blobs, leases, builds and generation.
